newsitem.title: USA: Midcoast sees pipeline deal accretive. [CORRECTED 21:43 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Midcoast sees pipeline deal accretive. [CORRECTED 21:43 GMT]

text.p: Midcoast Energy Resources Inc Chief Executive Officer Dan Tutcher on Wednesday said the company expects its acquisition of Atrion Corp pipeline assets to be accretive to earnings this year.

On a pro forma basis taking into account expected cost savings from the $41.4 million deal, Midcoast would have generated $12 million to $13 million in cash flow and $7.5 million or about $3.97 a share net income last year, he said.
Midcoast, a Houston-based pipeline company operating primarily in Texas and nine southeast states, posted $1.9 million or $1 a share on $3.4 million (company corrects) cash flow last year.
The company, which went public in August 1986, will finance the acquisition with bank debt and have a 76 percent debt-to-equity ratio after closing the deal, Tutcher said.
Midcoast entered into a definitive agreement to acquire the natural gas pipeline and energy marketing subsidiaries of Atrion in a deal that will more than double its asset base.

Tutcher said he expects to cut operating costs of the Atrion pipeline system and sees opportunities to boost revenues from the newly acquired assets after closing the deal late in the second quarter. "We find a lot of the things have been underutilized, underworked," he told Reuters.
